hints: Focus on what keeps a radical chain going, a radical must be used up and a brand new radical must be made.
Remember the two classic propagation steps for ethane are $\text{Cl} \bullet$ abstracting H to make $\text{HCl}$ plus an alkyl radical, then that radical reacting with $\text{Cl}_2$.
Check each equation for radical balance and for sensible radicals, $\text{H} \bullet$ is too unstable to form and two radicals joining is termination, not propagation.
walkthrough:
**Recall what propagation means**

Think of propagation as passing the baton. You start with one radical and one stable molecule, and you must finish with one stable molecule and one new radical.

Rule to check:
$$\text{radical + molecule} \rightarrow \text{molecule + radical}$$

**Recall the normal chlorination chain for ethane**

Initiation makes $\text{Cl} \bullet$. Then propagation keeps cycling.

Typical first propagation steps:
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_6 + \text{Cl} \bullet \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_5 \bullet + \text{HCl}$$
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5 \bullet + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl} + \text{Cl} \bullet$$

**Allow for further chlorination**

Once $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}$ is formed, it can be attacked again by $\text{Cl} \bullet$ in exactly the same H-abstraction way to move toward dichloroethanes.

That gives:
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl} + \text{Cl} \bullet \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{Cl} \bullet + \text{HCl}$$

**Test the other equations**

Any step that makes $\text{H} \bullet$ is invalid because $\text{H} \bullet$ is far too high in energy to form here. Any step with radical + radical joining to make a molecule is termination, because the radicals are removed.

options.A: Incorrect. Although it starts correctly with $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6 + \text{Cl} \bullet$, it claims to make $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl} + \text{H} \bullet$. Propagation by $\text{Cl} \bullet$ abstracts H to make $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5 \bullet$, it never ejects a free $\text{H} \bullet$.
options.B: Correct. This is radical + molecule going to molecule + radical, so the chain continues. $\text{Cl} \bullet$ abstracts a hydrogen from $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}$ to give $\text{HCl}$ and the new radical $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{Cl} \bullet$. This is a valid further-chlorination propagation step.
options.C: Incorrect. It uses $\text{H} \bullet$ as a reactant. $\text{H} \bullet$ is not produced in chlorination of ethane, so it cannot be available to propagate the chain. Students sometimes accept any balanced radical equation, but the radicals must be ones actually present.
options.D: Incorrect. This is $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5 \bullet + \text{Cl} \bullet \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}$. Two radicals combine to give one stable molecule with no new radical, so the chain is stopped. That is the definition of a termination step, not propagation.
